Task: 1 St Thomas Street Bronte- Sewer Dig Up
Invoice Description:

As the affected stack runs through the concrete stairs, relining would be the most cost effective solution to rectify this section of common sewer pipework.

  1. Notify residents of excavation works required on the right hand side of the building & water disruptions. 
  2. Install safety barricades around work area.
  3. Excavate trees within the garden bed.
  4. Saw cut concrete approximately 2 meters, excavate concrete using jack hammer and ground exposing the tree root infested/collapsed section of earthenware sewer piping and fittings.
  5. Turn off water supply and drain the water from the line.
  6. Cut out approximately 2 meters of tree root infested and collapsed section of earthenware sewer pipework, junction and fittings.
  7. Supply and install new PVC piping, fittings, junction connecting onto existing common sewer piping and install inspection opening at the base of the stack.
  8. Use CCTV drain camera downstream and ensure all clear.
  9. Turn on the water supply and flow test all works carried out.
  10. Bed pipework, back fill trench and compact fill as per AS 3500.
  11. Re-concrete affected common area.
  12. Remove associated rubbish, materials and fill from the property.
  13. Clean all areas where work had taken place with a high pressure hose.
  • Reline the base of the sewer stack on the right hand side of the building outside unit 1

- Preparation

  1. Advise affected residents of water disruptions. 
  2. Set up relining equipment on the right hand side of the building. 
  3. Use high pressure water jet blaster, mechanical milling tool, sanding paddles and CCTV drain camera to clean the pipework in preparation for relining. 
  4. CCTV camera record sewer line before relining.
  5. Measure, cut and prepare new line.

Attended the property, gained access under the building and found the common cold water isolation valve located under unit 1 to be leaking and required replacement.

Investigated fluctuating hot water supply to the building.

Gained access into the hot water heater room, found the common Rinnai 28i instantaneous hot water heater to show error code 10 on the control panel. Removed the air intake fan and removed large build up of dust and debris causing blockages. Cleaned out all dust and debris and re-installed. Tested common hot water heater and after 5 minutes the hot water heater would still cut out and error 10 code would appear on the control panel.

Returned to the property, engaged a hot water specialist contractor and carried out further investigation works to locate the fault.

We found the heater leaking in fault error 10; related to blocked flue. Dismantled flue to clean as well as terminal and fan internals; some build up but nothing overly excessive - Tested heater and it went into fault error 12; relates to flame failure; gas, supply pressure tested okay. 

Inspected and cleaned flame rods, again only not minor build up; tested to same error. Continued through heater diagnostic and found that the internal computer settings were set for use with a long flue (over 7 metres), this flue is only 2-3 metres long. We have changed the settings and the heater has fired up without fail for over 20 minutes. Due to incorrect settings, the fan would be too powerful for the flue length and it was likely causing uneven flame across the burner tray and flame rods.

Left heater on and rising in temperature; this incorrect setting is an obvious fault and is the likely cause of the recent issues. No other apparent causes have been identified during the service.

Shut down the buildings water supply and drained the water from the line.

Gained access under the building, disconnected faulty common isolation valve located under unit 1 and installed new isolation valve. Turned on the buildings cold water supply and tested all works carried out - All in good working order.

Cleaned all areas where work had taken place and removed associated rubbish from the property.

Task: 5 Ocean St Woollahra - no hot water
Invoice Description:
Investigate no hot water to the building.

Urgently attended the property on the 7/10 at 3.00pm, gained access into the buildings hot water plant room and found no hot water to the building.

The Rinnai hot water heater was faulting with the error code 12 indicating flame failure.

Disconnected water and power supply to the heater, disconnected and removed flame rods. Cleaned flame rods and re-installed, also removed water filter and cleaned.

Reconnected water and power supply to the Rinnai heater and tested. Rinnai heater found to be running for 5 minutes then faulting with error code 10, indicating a fault with the flue.

Inspected the flue and found no blockages. Removed outer flue layer - air intake. Re-set Rinnai heater and found no further fault codes indicating a fault with the flue.

Heater now up to temperature providing hot water to the building.

Returned to the property on the 9/10 and met with Rinnai Service technician. Rinnai Service Team carried out a full service of the hot water unit.

Internal combustion fan was completely blocked, replaced combustion fan, internal unit and combustion chamber was dirty causing obstructions, cleaned internal unit and combustion chamber, removing dirt. Serviced flame rods and relaced flame rod washers.

Re-connected flue piping and secured flue to the ceiling by fixing brackets.

Urgently returned to the property after hours on the 14/10 at 5.00pm, gained access and found no hot water to one of the units.

Inspected the Rinnai hot water heater and found it to be at working temperature 75 degrees. Carried out further investigations and found hot water return line to be cold. Removed return line pump, ran water flow bleeding air from the line. Tested and found the return line up to temperature.

Returned to the property on the 15/10, 8.00 am and found the return line pipework to be warm. Removed pump, ran water flow and there was no air in the line.

Following 2 x separate hot water outages within a few days, we found the Rinnai hot water heater required a complete service, the return line circulation pump is inadequate circulating cold/warm water throughout the building, and the Rinnai hot water heater flue is too long, according to the manufactures specifications.  

Further works required to be undertaken - To prevent further hot water outages at the building we advise a hot water specialist such as Paul Read or Cervas hot water is engaged to provide an URGENT quotation to completely upgrade the entire hot water plant and equipment at the building.
